_comment: The federal T2, structure-first. The Part I flow and the small business deduction, which is where proration for a short tax year first bites. Schedules and GIFI are not here yet.

checks.message: The business limit has been reduced for a short tax year.
checks.help: ITA 125(5) prorates the limit by the days in the tax year over 365. A first or final year is usually short.

checks.message: This tax year falls in two calendar years, so the rates have been apportioned by days.
checks.help: A fiscal period crossing a calendar boundary is taxed at each year's rates in proportion to the days falling in it, rather than at whichever year the period mostly occupies.

checks.message: Schedule 1 covers the common reconciling items only.
checks.help: Reserves, resource deductions, scientific research expenditures and several other items are not modelled. Anything missing can be entered as an other addition or deduction, but the return will not compute it for you.

checks.message: Part of the charitable donations could not be deducted this year.
checks.help: The deduction is capped at a share of net income. The excess carries forward, which Freshet does not track yet.

checks.message: This tax year is a loss for tax purposes.
checks.help: No tax is payable. The loss may be carried back or forward, which Freshet does not track yet.

checks.message: No small business deduction has been claimed.
checks.help: Active business income has been left at nil, so the small business deduction is nil and this income is taxed at the general rate. That is right for a corporation whose income is investment income, and wrong for most others: a CCPC carrying on an active business should enter that income to claim the deduction.

lines.label: Net income per the financial statements
lines.note: GIFI line 9999. The return starts from the accounts rather than from a figure entered separately, which is the point of filing the statements with it.

lines.label: Provision for income taxes
lines.note: GIFI line 9990. Income tax is not deductible in computing income for tax purposes, so the accounting provision comes straight back.

lines.label: Amortization and depreciation
lines.note: GIFI line 8670. Accounting amortization is added back in full and replaced by capital cost allowance, which is deducted below.

lines.label: Non-deductible portion of meals and entertainment
lines.note: ITA 67.1 allows half. The parameter is the *deductible* share and the addback is what is left, written that way because the Act states the deductible half rather than the disallowed one.

lines.label: Fines, penalties and club dues
lines.note: ITA 67.6 disallows fines and penalties outright; ITA 18(1)(l) disallows dues for a club whose main purpose is dining, recreation or sport.

lines.label: Charitable donations added back
lines.note: Donations are an expense in the accounts but are not deducted in computing income. They come back here and are deducted from taxable income instead, where a limit applies.

lines.label: Total additions
lines.note: Recapture is included here: selling an asset for more than its remaining undepreciated cost means past capital cost allowance was too generous, and the excess comes back into income.

lines.label: Capital cost allowance
lines.note: Schedule 8, computed from the shared capital cost allowance fragment — the same pool arithmetic a T1 uses for a sole proprietor, because it is the same statute.

lines.label: Total deductions
lines.note: Terminal loss is included here: retiring the last asset in a class for less than its remaining undepreciated cost means past capital cost allowance was too stingy, and the shortfall is deducted.

lines.label: Net income for income tax purposes
lines.note: Schedule 1 reconciles the accounting result to this. It may be negative — a loss is a real outcome, so this line is not floored.

lines.label: Charitable donations deducted
lines.note: ITA 110.1(1): capped at a share of net income, so a corporation that donated more than it earned carries the excess forward rather than creating a loss with it.

lines.label: Taxable income
lines.note: Net income less the charitable donations deduction and other deductions such as loss carryforwards.

lines.label: Active business income
lines.note: Income from an active business carried on in Canada. Investment income does not qualify for the small business deduction, which is the whole reason this is separate from taxable income.

lines.label: Business limit, prorated for a short tax year
lines.note: ITA 125(5): the limit is reduced by the number of days in the tax year over 365. A corporation with a short first year gets a fraction of it. The 365 is written here rather than derived from the calendar because the Act says 365 even in a leap year — reading 366 off the calendar would over-claim.

lines.label: Small business deduction
lines.note: ITA 125(1): the rate applied to the least of active business income, taxable income and the business limit.

lines.label: Base amount of Part I tax
lines.note: ITA 123(1): 38% of taxable income. Apportioned by days if the fiscal period straddles a rate change — which is why it is a blended parameter and the business limit, an amount the Act fixes for the year rather than a rate in force on a day, is not.

lines.label: Federal tax abatement
lines.note: ITA 124(1): 10% of taxable income earned in a province, which is what leaves room for provincial corporate tax.

lines.label: General tax reduction
lines.note: ITA 123.4: available on income that did not already get the small business deduction, so the two do not stack.
